subject: Escalation: Dedicated rollout-related latency spikes + request for staged rollouts / audit trail (SUP-3917, SUP-3924, SUP-3981)
body:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 30, 2025 at 9:18 AM PST
Subject: Escalation: Dedicated rollout-related latency spikes + request for staged rollouts / audit trail (SUP-3917, SUP-3924, SUP-3981)

Lauren / Marissa / Marcus — escalating a cluster of Dedicated customer asks that are now gating a renewal + expansion.

What we’re seeing:
- SUP-3917: Dedicated tenant reports model update caused p95 latency spikes + queue depth growth in their reserved pool.
- SUP-3924: Confusion about what “traffic split” means today during model update (they assumed safe canary; we essentially did pool-level cutover).
- SUP-3981: Compliance team asking for auditable approvals trail (who approved / when / what changed) for any model/runtime/config rollout action.

Support (Dev) can keep doing manual steps, but customers are pushing back on the risk profile.

Ask:
1) Can we align on a single customer-facing message on timeline + what’s included in beta vs GA for “Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools” (PM-418)?
2) Interim guidance: what do we tell customers to do *now* when they need to roll a model version safely on Dedicated? (e.g., time window + traffic draining, capacity headroom, “clone pool” option, etc.)
3) For audit: can we commit to an “approvals + audit events” story for enterprise security reviews (even if UI is later)?

I need to send an update to two accounts by EOD tomorrow with something concrete.

Thanks,
Rachel

—
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Customer Success Lead
Redwood Inference


----

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 30, 2025 at 10:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation: Dedicated rollout-related latency spikes + request for staged rollouts / audit trail (SUP-3917, SUP-3924, SUP-3981)

+1 escalating. This is exactly the Dedicated risk we’ve been worried about: pool saturation during “all-at-once” rollouts.

On interim guidance (what customers can do today):
- We should recommend “maintenance window” + manual hold points + explicit rollback plan.
- We can also suggest temporarily reducing max concurrency / tightening rate limits during the change.
- For a couple customers we can offer a second reserved pool or a short-term burst pool for canary (but that’s an ops-heavy exception).

Marissa — can you share what we’re comfortable committing to for beta? My preference is to be very explicit that v1 is operator-driven / allowlisted, not fully self-serve.

Rachel — if you send me the two account names (privately is fine) I can help tailor the wording re: Dedicated constraints.

Lauren

—
Lauren Bishop
Product, Dedicated
Redwood Inference


----

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 30, 2025 at 11:11 AM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation: Dedicated rollout-related latency spikes + request for staged rollouts / audit trail (SUP-3917, SUP-3924, SUP-3981)

Thanks — agree we need a consistent message.

Current plan for PM-418 (Dedicated staged rollouts):
- Beta target: starting ~Week 9–10 of the project plan (we’re tracking toward mid/late March for first customer enablement, assuming dogfood doesn’t uncover major issues).
- Scope for beta:
  - Multi-stage rollout plan on a Dedicated pool (e.g., 5% -> 25% -> 100%)
  - Gates on core reliability metrics (p95 latency, 5xx, timeouts, queue depth, GPU utilization) with “fail-safe hold” on missing/late metrics
  - Manual approvals at stage boundaries (operator-driven)
  - Audit events emitted for create/update/approve/abort/auto-hold (Marcus’ area)
  - Console visibility is included, but we may have some rough edges (status consistency + refresh behavior)
- Explicit exclusions for beta:
  - General customer self-serve (initially Redwood-operated + allowlist)
  - Complex experimentation / bandits (separate)
  - Quality gating for all workloads (optional / limited)

If we want to be conservative in customer comms, I’d position this as:
- “Private beta for select Dedicated enterprise tenants”
- “Operator-managed at first, with auditability and controls suitable for change management”

Rachel — I’d recommend offering a check-in with Product + CS + Support to walk through “safe manual rollout” steps until staged rollouts are available.

Marissa

—
Marissa Cole
Product Lead, Console & Rollouts
Redwood Inference


----

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 30, 2025 at 12:03 PM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation: Dedicated rollout-related latency spikes + request for staged rollouts / audit trail (SUP-3917, SUP-3924, SUP-3981)

On audit trail: we can (and should) commit to an approval + audit logging story for enterprise.

What I’m comfortable stating externally (with careful wording):
- All staged rollout actions will emit immutable audit events (create/update/approve/abort/auto-hold) with actor identity, timestamp, tenant + pool identifiers, and “what changed”.
- Events will be available via our existing audit log export pipeline (for customers with audit export enabled).

What I would *not* commit to yet:
- Specific retention windows unless we align with the customer’s contract + our standard policy.
- “SOC2 evidence” language beyond what we already provide.

Rachel — if you share which customers are asking, I can help craft a paragraph for their security reviewer that stays within approved claims.

Marcus

—
Marcus Lin
Security Lead
Redwood Inference


----

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 30, 2025 at 2:27 PM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation: Dedicated rollout-related latency spikes + request for staged rollouts / audit trail (SUP-3917, SUP-3924, SUP-3981)

Super helpful, thank you.

Accounts (keeping this thread internal):
- Account A: renewal in Feb; escalation is SUP-3917 (rollout caused queue depth/latency spike) + they want staged rollout controls as condition for expansion.
- Account B: security review in progress; escalation is SUP-3981 (audit trail of approvals).

Proposed customer-facing message (please sanity-check):
1) Today: Dedicated rollouts are pool-level changes; Redwood can run a “manual staged rollout” procedure (timeboxed, explicit rollback, temporary concurrency limits, additional monitoring).
2) Near-term: We’re building first-class “Dedicated staged rollouts” with deterministic traffic shifting + metric-based gates; private beta for select Dedicated enterprise customers in March; GA to follow after beta learnings.
3) Audit: staged rollout actions will be captured in audit logs (actor, timestamp, action, tenant/pool identifiers). Availability via audit export for customers with that feature enabled.

If OK, I’ll send this tomorrow and offer a joint call.

Rachel


----

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 31, 2025 at 9:06 AM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation: Dedicated rollout-related latency spikes + request for staged rollouts / audit trail (SUP-3917, SUP-3924, SUP-3981)

Your proposed message looks good.

Two small tweaks to keep us safe:
- Instead of “in March” say “targeting March” / “as early as March” (we still need dogfood + SRE sign-off).
- For GA, avoid dates; say “following beta and operational readiness”.

If Account A needs a stronger commitment, we can offer:
- “We will prioritize you for the private beta” (if they’re willing to be allowlisted and accept operator-managed rollouts initially).

Marissa


----

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 31, 2025 at 9:41 AM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation: Dedicated rollout-related latency spikes + request for staged rollouts / audit trail (SUP-3917, SUP-3924, SUP-3981)

+1 to Marissa’s wording.

For the audit paragraph, suggested language you can paste:

“Staged rollout actions (e.g., plan updates, stage approvals, aborts, and automatic holds triggered by gate conditions) are recorded as audit events with actor identity and timestamps, and can be exported via Redwood’s audit log export for customers with audit export enabled.”

Avoid saying “immutable” externally unless we’re in a formal security response.

Marcus


----

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 3, 2025 at 4:07 PM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation: Dedicated rollout-related latency spikes + request for staged rollouts / audit trail (SUP-3917, SUP-3924, SUP-3981)

Update: I sent the revised note (“targeting March” + no GA dates) and both accounts accepted the plan.

Next steps requested by Account A:
- They want a 30-min working session this week on the interim “manual staged rollout” procedure + what metrics we’ll gate on in beta.

Marissa/Lauren — can you each join 15 min of that call? I’ll have Support run the procedural part; we mainly need to confirm the staged rollout semantics (weights, holds, approvals) and set expectations.

Marcus — FYI security reviewer for Account B asked whether approvals are role-restricted. I told them we’re implementing RBAC controls for approve/abort/edit, initially operator-scoped with tenant-scoped controls later.

Thanks again for the fast turnaround.

Rachel
